title: Exploring the Use of ChatGPT in Chinese Language Classrooms
venue: International Journal of Chinese Language Teaching
extended_summary:
This paper examines how ChatGPT can be used as an instructional support tool in Chinese language teaching across three university-level courses. The central question is how ChatGPT might enhance learning, feedback, and assessment in Chinese language classrooms while remaining aligned with course objectives, institutional AI guidance, and backward design principles. The paper is motivated by practical teaching challenges such as varied student proficiency, limited instructor time for individualized feedback, and the need for more opportunities for writing and dialogue practice.

The paper describes three course implementations rather than a controlled comparison study. In an Intermediate-Low Chinese course, ChatGPT was used as a conversation partner, vocabulary expansion tool, and source of cultural information for written dialogue practice. In an Intermediate-High Chinese course, students wrote narrative drafts and compared their own writing with ChatGPT-revised versions, focusing especially on time connectors, coherence, vocabulary, and fluency. In a Chinese for Academic Purposes course for native or near-native speakers, ChatGPT was used for self-diagnosis, draft evaluation, revision support, and workshop-style feedback on titles, introductions, and outlines using instructor-provided criteria.

The population consisted of undergraduate students at the University of Toronto Mississauga in Canada across three Chinese courses: 13 students in the intermediate-low course, 7 students in the intermediate-high course, and 30 students in the academic writing course. The setting was classroom-based higher education instruction, with activities integrated into regular coursework. The paper also reports instructor reflections and some examples of student reactions, emphasizing the use of ChatGPT as a peer-like assistant rather than an authoritative evaluator.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT can support Chinese language learning by providing flexible, immediate, and personalized assistance for dialogue practice, writing revision, and formative assessment. The authors argue that it can enrich classroom learning and promote student reflection and critical thinking when used carefully. At the same time, they note limitations such as repetitive or potentially incorrect responses, reading difficulty for some learners, and the risk that students may become overly reliant on AI-generated writing support. The paper does not provide experimental evidence of effectiveness relative to other tools or comparison conditions, so its contribution is primarily descriptive and practice-oriented rather than causal.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive classroom report with instructor reflections and illustrative examples rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparative study. It offers some empirical classroom detail and sample sizes, but lacks a clear causal design, validated outcome measurement, and statistical analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests beneficial but unclear impact on writing, language practice, critical thinking, and efficiency; however, impacts are not quantified and no effect sizes are reported. Relevance to the requested high-school direct-comparison topic is limited because the study is postsecondary, single-arm, and does not compare ChatGPT against legacy automated writing tools or hybrid workflows.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT is used across three university Chinese language courses as a conversational and instructional partner for grammar practice, dialogue interaction, draft revision, rubric-aligned writing feedback, and self-reflective discussion about revisions.

In the intermediate-high and academic Chinese writing courses, ChatGPT is used specifically as a writing assistance tool to revise student drafts, comment on vocabulary/grammar/cohesion, and provide rubric- or guideline-based feedback for revision.
Students input writing criteria or ACTFL-based expectations into ChatGPT and receive automated evaluations and revision suggestions on drafts, outlines, titles, and introductions.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports instructor and anecdotal student reflections suggesting ChatGPT supported writing-related outcomes in intermediate-high and academic Chinese courses, including improved use of time connectors, coherence, vocabulary, grammar, and revision quality. However, no experimental comparison, validated rubric scores, inter-rater reliability statistics, or effect sizes are reported; evidence consists of descriptive classroom examples with class sizes of 7 and 30 in the writing-focused courses.
finding.measure: Instructor reflections, classroom activities, anecdotal student feedback, draft comparison tasks, and descriptive references to ACTFL-aligned writing criteria

finding.finding_summary: In the intermediate-low Chinese class, instructors report that ChatGPT supported written dialogue practice, vocabulary expansion, question formation, grammar application, reading comprehension, and confidence in communication. These claims are based on narrative reflection from a class of 13 students rather than direct pre/post language proficiency testing or controlled comparison.
finding.measure: Instructor and student reflections on dialogue practice, vocabulary/grammar use, and confidence during written conversational tasks

finding.finding_summary: Across the three course examples, the authors describe ChatGPT as fostering critical thinking, reflection, self-assessment, and autonomous learning by prompting students to compare drafts, evaluate AI suggestions, and make revision decisions. The academic writing workshop example especially emphasizes metacognitive reflection on accepting or rejecting ChatGPT feedback, but no standardized durable-skills measures or quantitative estimates are provided.
finding.measure: Reflective writing tasks, self-assessment activities, comparative evaluation of peer vs ChatGPT feedback, and instructor observations of critical thinking/metacognition
finding.study_size: n=13; n=7; n=30 across three course contexts

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that ChatGPT improved instructional efficiency by providing immediate, individualized feedback and enabling simultaneous one-to-one interaction that instructors could not feasibly provide, especially in larger writing classes. These efficiency claims are plausible and grounded in classroom implementation descriptions, but no formal workload, time-on-task, or productivity metrics are reported.
finding.measure: Descriptive reports of immediacy of feedback, scalability of one-to-one support, and perceived reduction of instructional bottlenecks

finding.finding_summary: The paper discusses how ChatGPT use was aligned with institutional AI guidelines and course design principles, indicating a supportive governance context for classroom adoption. This is not evaluated as an institutional outcome with comparative data, but it provides descriptive evidence of policy-guided implementation rather than ad hoc use.
finding.measure: Narrative description of institutional AI guidance and compliance in course design
